category_notes.text: Invoke’s current primary site describes a layered generation canvas. Today’s Infinite Canvas and local inspiration-library guides distinguish the interface, chosen inference provider and model/asset permissions.

OpenReelio and Kaestral describe agent-assisted editing of actual footage. Phosphene’s current changelog advertises 5.0.19 but also retains older highlighted release text; its Pro features must not be attributed to the free route. The existing full guide is preserved; the current release has not been reviewed into a new guide.

OpenSuno describes local YuE2 music, while the new Voicebox and MusicStudio guides cover speech and song work. MusicStudio’s separate SongBench academic restriction is excluded from its assessed generation/mastering route.

SolidCraft’s current site describes agent-operated parametric CAD and warns about pre-release compatibility. New guides distinguish editable solids, generated props and learned captures; these outputs do not certify fabrication.
The WebLLM primary paper supplies browser-inference context. Three-Live, browser OCR, style transfer and stem separation require their own backend/device and model-term checks.
Meta’s agentic Immersive Web SDK article and the current Three-Live sources broaden runtime-scene discovery. Native AR, browser WebXR and a static GLB/USDZ handoff preserve different interactions.

Fragment’s current site describes shader/canvas/MIDI creative coding. Conventional rendering is not automatically an AI tool; dedicated external-agent authoring integrations are identified explicitly.
ossia’s current installation documentation covers sensor-to-media control. LivePose’s actual neural inference-to-OSC path is separate from its optional proprietary creative hosts.

SOMA and Kerfline describe agent/CAD and AI-assisted laser-pattern workflows. New FreeCAD and KiCad guides retain separate geometric, electrical, slicer, material and physical-output checks; a digital export is not fabrication approval.

ForgeAX’s primary documentation describes agent-directed game authoring, inspectable previews and specialist planning roles. An agent framework, game runtime and generated assets have distinct evidence and permission needs.
Movens-Zero’s author site describes multimodal motion generation. Dataset/model release terms and reproducibility must be reviewed independently of its demonstration film.
The current AVTR-1 model page exposes a community weight license. Downloadable avatar weights are not necessarily open-source software or unrestricted commercial assets.

A readable primary light-aware-compositing paper supplies neural illumination-aware insertion context. Its paper examples alone do not establish a licensed released application or successful production integration.

A neural-acoustic-fields PDF was bounded and unreadable as a full document. Its accessible NSF record describes learned spatial reverberation/viewpoint synthesis; this is publication context, not a complete code or hardware review.

The primary volumetric-capture paper describes learned RGB/RGB-D reconstruction. MosaicEarth’s Gaussian-scene workflow and Open Reality’s VGGT capture have different compute, geometry and model constraints; phone/browser capture does not imply lightweight backend inference.

Subtitle Edit’s current documentation supplies assisted-caption context. Today’s subtitle and video guides distinguish local helpers, semantic model review, remote transcription and optional proprietary editing hosts.
The SVGRender author organization describes differentiable vector rendering. Conventional SVG conversion alone is not AI; a concrete learned or agent-assisted creative operation is required.
The VecGlypher primary paper supplies neural glyph-design context. Font-data rights, exported font validity and current code permissions are separate checks.

The dramai page yielded only a site shell and its docs path returned 404. Today’s actual FrameStage and Sympoiesis source reviews provide story/poem workflows without treating those failed site reads as complete documentation.

OpenSlides failed with an SSL protocol error. The accessible official manimvox documentation describes agent-researched, narrated Manim explainers; its failed custom-domain attempt remains a separate gap. No unchanged package guide is recycled.
The primary autochrome-restoration paper describes a specific neural recovery problem. Newly reviewed local image/archival tools are not granted broad restoration or color-fidelity claims.
The DL4SciVis primary survey supplies learned visualization context; narrated charts and a scientific figure require factual/source checks beyond a successful renderer.

MIT Illuminate describes an interactive artwork rather than a newly licensed reusable app. New LenoxVI room-voice and Pi-KI pose-to-MIDI guides expose actual speech/vision-to-sound paths with specific hardware limitations.

ossia’s projection page and SAT’s current Koaia/LivePose documentation distinguish conventional media control, neural visual effects and learned pose-to-OSC. Current SAT build subscriptions and model terms remain separate from source grants.

OpenTryOn describes a model registry, not universal model permission. Today’s AI Fashion Inspo guide scopes neural tagging/search to manually uploaded, permission-cleared images; optional face/try-on models require their own terms and validation.
W3C’s primary visual-description guidance informs media review. OCR, subtitle translation and pose systems need editorial/user checks, not automatic accuracy claims.

Google’s Android segmentation documentation supplies edge-inference context. The browser and Pi workflows in this edition retain explicit device/runtime requirements; a web UI does not establish native phone or Mac model support.

The KinoDraw primary URL returned 404. Accessible manimvox documentation supplies an adjacent narrated-education workflow; this is an explicit source gap, not evidence of no tools or a validated new release.
PyPottery’s primary documentation covers pottery-image and drawing workflows. Neural enhancement, OCR and organization must retain source imagery and provenance rather than overwrite evidence.

MAESTRO’s author page and official multimodal task pages extend music-to-dance, language/vision and sentence-embedding search vocabulary. Fields are open-ended; project-site coverage is not evidence that every checkpoint has open software/model terms.
TouchTwin’s primary paper describes language/touch authoring for scanned scenes. A published system description does not establish public software, haptic hardware access or a reusable open grant.

NeRAF’s author site describes joint visual/acoustic fields, while AudioStellar’s current GitLab README describes corpus-map performance. The NSF publication summary supplements an unreadable bounded PDF; complete software/model and realtime readiness are separate.
OpenMagia’s current primary site describes a local media studio. New agent-tool guides identify the real model/agent step rather than mislabel deterministic rendering as generative inference.
LyriFont’s student project page documents music/lyric-driven visual typography. Research/art provenance is context, not an automatic maturity or quality label.
MAESTRO’s current primary site describes structure-aware music-to-dance generation and editing. The public demo and any released code require separate software/model and motion-quality checks.
ARK Lab’s Ink Blossom page describes AI-assisted traditional embroidery interaction. An installation description is not proof of a downloadable, machine-ready embroidery tool.
TMD Studio’s live page includes a Basic Pitch hum-to-score route; Algomus’s primary co-composition source supplies another ecosystem. MIDI/score correctness and model permissions remain separate.
The AEGIR author site still labels code as coming soon. Its inverse-rendering results are a research lead, not an eligible released tool without code and a reviewed grant.

AromaGen’s primary paper describes multimodal LLM-to-scent authoring with a twelve-channel wearable device. A research publication does not clear its software, scent materials or a safe reusable exhibition setup.
AgenticCAD’s current site describes free non-commercial use, a restriction requiring full software-grant review rather than automatic open-source admission.
AEGIR and neural-light-field research broaden light/view-dependent terminology. Paper novelty does not establish a deployable display-authoring app or a cleared code license.

The Neural Puppet primary paper supplies learned-character context. A research video and available character assets do not establish a current reusable software grant or support for every proprietary rig.
PyPotteryTrace’s current primary guide covers pottery drawing/vector workflows. AI inference, conventional tracing and archaeological interpretation must be distinguished.
The AgenticCAD primary site exposes non-commercial conditions. New open-code CAD candidates keep geometric checks, mechanical fit and manufacturing proof separate.

The MapStory PDF capture was size-bounded and unreadable as a complete document, and the referenced project page returned 404. Map-animation discovery remains supplemented by repository queries; no full paper, code or runtime review is claimed from these captures.

FORM’s author page describes material-parameter learning and robot shaping. That research is adjacent context; neither the page nor a rendered design establishes authorization, safe physical execution or a cleared creator application.

OpenToonz’s current primary site describes open animation production. Actual neural or agent-assisted features must be evidenced separately; conventional cel software is not admitted merely by association.
FolAI’s primary site still says code available soon. Its synchronized sound examples remain research context until a public implementation and grant are reviewed.
The TQCodec primary paper supplies learned music-codec context. Codec research does not by itself establish a usable creative app or open checkpoint permissions.
Sonify’s Parallax page documents an actual neural-art/data-sonification collaboration. An artwork and its production tools are different evidence targets.
Google Research’s Brain2Music page describes reconstruction from fMRI. It is adjacent neural-media research, not evidence of a consumer EEG authoring tool.
VideoNeuMat’s author page describes extracting neural materials from video-model data. Training/reconstruction code, material rights and DCC compatibility need separate review.
The NeuralCameras PDF was bounded and did not yield a readable full document. This remains an explicit access gap; no full-paper or source-license approval is claimed.
Learn2Fold’s primary record describes structured origami generation. Digital fold plans are not proof of material feasibility, mechanical safety or a cleared downloadable implementation.
OpenCADIrrigation’s primary page describes an AI assistant; LibreTerrain’s live GitLab README supplies conventional terrain context. A terrain node graph is not automatically AI.
Visual Anagrams’ author page documents diffusion-based optical illusions. A visually plausible mosaic/illusion does not establish fabrication or printing readiness.
The Visual Anagrams primary gallery supplies concrete perceptual-transformation context. New candidates still need original-code and model-license review.

Imprimatur’s current site describes relief-roller generation and an open hardware grant. A conventional image-to-relief tool alone is not a new AI tool; learned halftone candidates were screened separately.
The Birth of a Painting primary paper describes differentiable brushstroke reconstruction. Research images do not establish a licensed production painting app.
HueForge Studio’s primary docs describe palette/color editing and a distinct AI-generation feature. Conventional recoloring and model-backed generation have different dependencies.

The Library of Congress’s primary collage experiment explicitly uses computer vision for cut-and-paste exploration of collection imagery. Collection/object rights and segmentation evidence remain separate.
The primary stereoscopic neural-style-transfer paper supplies binocular-consistency context. Stereo conversion and a valid 3D export are not interchangeable claims.

The actual Semantic Gaussians author page describes projected neural features, open-vocabulary segmentation and language-guided Gaussian-scene editing. The earlier neighboring URL returned 404; full implementation and dependency-grant review remain pending.
PHOSA’s current author page says code coming soon and names Deaf-co-designed evaluation. A research avatar demo is not a cleared open signing tool or validated translation system.

TONE3000 and GitLab’s embedded amp experiment provide neural-DSP context. The new apresta neural~ lead is an MIT Max amplifier-model player. IRCAM’s similarly named nn~ has a non-commercial software grant and is excluded; neither a popular name nor a downloadable model replaces full license review.
World-Shaper’s primary page describes geometry-aware 360-degree editing. Spherical consistency, model rights and runtime memory require workflow-specific evidence.
The author’s learning-based clothing page links released code/models. Training-data, garment and downstream simulation rights remain distinct from the paper.

X-Dub’s primary page mixes a released-code announcement with language about preparing source release. This conflict needs an actual repository check. Today’s PersoDub guide keeps translation providers, voices, lips and local hardware distinct.
The official Morphic model card supplies camera-reshooting context and its own model metadata. A downloadable LoRA is not a blanket software/model grant.

Intel OIDN’s current site and Blender’s primary sampling manual describe learned denoising and optional GPU acceleration. Prefiltering/quality modes trade detail for time; a different device path or a new page date does not automatically upgrade an existing assessment.

A primary codec/deepfake paper and current TensorStack NuGet versions broaden quality-analysis discovery. A detector or file-based score cannot prove authenticity, audience success or artistic quality.
Imprimatur and learned-halftone sources distinguish conventional relief geometry from neural image processing. Neither a connected vector nor a binary pattern proves a successful printed edition.
AlayaWorld’s primary demo page describes interactive long-horizon video worlds. Frame rate and consistency claims remain author results until independently verified with released software.

The RAVE primary paper supplies learned latent-audio context. Today’s completed Patchkamer guide assesses its explicit external-agent device contract and validator; conventional synths in that studio are not mislabeled neural inference.
The primary Optica page was reachable but mostly exposes navigation/access messaging in the captured text. Complete paper/code access remains a gap; no new eligible tool is claimed.
The primary planetarium/LLM paper extends live-dome control vocabulary. SAT’s conventional dome viewers are not automatically new AI tools, and public show use needs its own runtime review.
StitchFoundry’s current primary site describes AI design assistance and sew-out review. A stitch file and a software claim do not prove a tested machine/material result.
The Imprimatur primary site supplies actual relief-printing context. Its open hardware status is separate from eligibility as an AI software tool.

Nasjonalmuseet’s local semantic-search account, ZKM’s Intelligent Museum source-code page and LinkedCulture’s prototype description supply institutional context. Today’s slop.gallery lead has actual AI-director source; gallery polish is not independent museum-deployment evidence.
The Eagle Animation site was reachable but yielded only a minimal shell. It does not establish an AI feature, full current documentation or a newly cleared open-source AI application.

SoundPlot’s primary record describes birdsong-analysis and interactive visualization but also references conventional Griffin-Lim/PCA components. Its title alone does not establish a released neural synthesis tool or clear ecological-data permissions.
LookingGlass’s primary paper describes generative anamorphoses via warping. Printed/viewing geometry and perceptual output need material-specific verification.
The Light Field Neural Rendering author site supplies multiview synthesis context. Neural view interpolation is not proof of a glasses-free display runtime or compatible hardware.

AstroSURE describes learned astronomical denoising. An attractive denoised image is not calibrated recovery of telescope measurements; instrument-specific validation, source data and software/model terms remain separate.
The primary tactile-graphics paper supplies text-to-relief context. Code availability, tactile readability, fabrication and evaluation with intended users remain separate gates.
UDnet’s primary gallery describes neural underwater color/contrast restoration. Appearance improvement must not be presented as calibrated recovery of lost scene colors.

A readable EUSIPCO paper describes a CNN predicting violin-plate vibration/acoustic fields from finite-element examples. This is learned acoustic modeling, distinct from optical holographic display authoring; no creator-app license is inferred.
CalliRewrite’s author page describes recovering handwriting behaviors from images. Learned trajectory output and executing a physical brush robot require different evidence.
ComicTL’s current site describes local detection/OCR/translation in a browser extension. It remains necessary to check the actual extension, model terms, typesetting and page rights.

ShopPrentice’s current site describes a furniture-design MCP service and paid assistant credits. A public service or editable cut list alone does not establish all source permissions or real joinery validation.
Taarib’s primary site describes agent-assisted removable translation patches. Underlying game rights, Arabic rendering and playable regression evidence remain distinct from open tool code.
LacyLights’ primary site provides current DMX/show-control context. Conventional Art-Net output is not itself AI; agent/MCP integration and actual cue behavior must be evidenced separately.

Music2P provides adjacent music-to-cover context. Today’s Memory Zine Book guide adds an actual agent/vision-assisted static photobook workflow, with original-photo preservation and an explicit distinction from print imposition or page-turn video.

WAIvePulse’s site describes song generation, mixing, looping and performance on local hardware. Today’s Attic, Cochlea and Sonic Bridge guides distinguish learned generation, external-agent composition and deterministic signal descriptors.
The primary inverse-knitting paper describes recovering procedural yarn structure from images. A neural yarn representation is not automatically a machine-knit instruction file.
